source.text: Jarro de agua fría a la ronda de cuartos de final del Masters 1000 ATP de Canadá. Un grupo de ocho jugadores que han hecho ya historia, ya que es la primera vez que tenistas nacidos en los años 2000 copan la antepenúltima ronda de un torneo de esta categoría. Rafa Jódar es el más joven con 19 años, siendo el estadounidense Brandon Nakashima el de mayor edad con 25. Sólo dos de los supervivientes tienen un M1000 en su palmares, el defensor de la corona en tierras canadienses, Ben Shelton, y su rival, el checo Jakub Mensik. El espectáculo comenzó da la peor manera posible. Después de varios retrasos en el horario de apertura de los cuartos, la jornada del lunes acabó siendo cancelada. Ni saltaron a la pista el español Rafa Jódar y el francés Arthur Fils, con cita a las 00:00 horas peninsular española, las 6 de la tarde en Montreal. A las dos y cuarto de la madrugada, 20:15 en el torneo, la organización anunció la suspensión definitiva de la jornada. El parte meteorológico y la hora tardía invitaron a ello. Además de Jódar y Fils, también se marcharon para el hotel el italiano Luciano Darderi y el estadounidense Brandon Nakashima. Los cuartos deberán celebrarse todos en una misma sesión, este martes, ya con menos margen porque el miércoles son las semifinales y el jueves, la final. Enseguida arranda el Masters 1000 ATP de Cincinnati. Para el martes ya estaba fijado el duelo del español Dani Mérida con el estadounidense Learner Tien y el choque de Ben Shelton y Jakub Mensik.
source.title: Cancelado el partido de cuartos de Jódar en Montreal

siteGuidance.onBeat: Any article whose title or content centers on the footballer Rodri (Rodrigo Hernández Cascante): his transfer rumors, injuries, match performances, national team involvement, contract/salary news, quotes from or about him, and how his situation affects Manchester City, Spain's national team, or transfer targets linking him to clubs like Real Madrid.
siteGuidance.offBeat: General transfer market roundups, other players' transfers and news, other sports (basketball, tennis, UFC, cycling, motorsport), lifestyle/foodie/leisure content, front-page image galleries, TV schedule listings, and club news unrelated to Rodri.

voiceGuide.guideRaw:
# Voice Guide: @ReshadRahman

## Beat & Scope

**Covers.** Everything tied directly to Rodri's transfer to Barcelona: bid and counter-bid figures between Manchester City and Barcelona, negotiation status (ongoing, stalled, breakthrough), personal terms and agreement stages, quotes from insider journalists relaying the story, the roles of Pep Guardiola, Hansi Flick and Deco in the deal, Rodri's own stated preference for Barcelona over Real Madrid, and financing moves that are explicitly linked to funding the Rodri deal (example below). Manchester City and Real Madrid appear only as counterparties/rivals in the Rodri story, never covered for their own sake. Barcelona figures (Flick, Deco) are treated as major; agents, unnamed "City sources," and outlets like SER are routine.

<post>
❗️The money which Barcelona was initially going to use for a CB will now be going into the signing of Rodri, reports SER. #Transfers 💰🚨
</post>

**Excludes.** Other players' transfers even when Barcelona is a party — filter these out even though they sit on the same account:

<post>
🚨🚨 BREAKING: Liverpool signs Araujo on loan! @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 💥💥
</post>

<post>
🚨 JUST IN: Cuti Romero to Barcelona depends on Barcelona. If the club decides to enter the race, they have space and still have the possibility to. All depends on the club. Right now, Cuti is negotiating with Atletico, but still no green light. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 🇦🇷
</post>

Also exclude generic Barcelona transfer targets with no Rodri connection, and personal/non-football asides:

<post>
New CB signing on the cards too? 👀☎️
</post>

<post>
anyways, good morning ☀️
</post>

**Edge cases.**
- A Barcelona signing whose budget is explicitly reallocated *from or to* the Rodri deal → **covers** (see the SER example above).
- A generic Barcelona CB or forward target with no stated Rodri link (e.g. "alternative to Julian") → **excludes**.
- Rodri's national-team/Ballon d'Or moments used as evidence inside a transfer post (e.g. a photo of him kissing a trophy under a "never wanted Real Madrid" post) → **covers**, because it serves the transfer narrative, not standalone Spain NT news.
- A personal, non-football aside from the writer ("not sleeping yet, just in case 😆") → **excludes**, even during an active Rodri news cycle.

## Identity & Register

Writing as a single-subject insider tracker in the Fabrizio Romano mould, but with exactly one player's move as the entire beat: Rodri to Barcelona. The audience already follows the saga day-to-day — never re-explain who Rodri, Barcelona, or Manchester City are, and never contextualize a fee or a name. The dominant register is a controlled news wire: short, declarative, sourced. A secondary register — used sparingly — is a calmer, first-person voice that predicts, reassures, or asks the audience a question directly. Judgment about the deal's merits belongs to quoted sources, never to the writer's own sentences.

## Hard Rules — Always

- **Open hard-news bulletins with 🚨 (optionally stacked with 💥/🔥/☎️) immediately followed by the caps label "JUST IN:" or "BREAKING:".**

<post>
🚨💥 JUST IN: Barcelona has begun putting the final touches to its first offer for Rodri. @rac1 #Transfers 💰🔵🔴⏳
</post>

- **Credit a named journalist with an @handle placed right after the fact and before the hashtag.**

<post>
🚨🔥 BREAKING: All contractual terms now ACCEPTED by Rodri. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 💰🔵🔴✅ https://t.co/xRQz1SZYAL
</post>
<media>Photo — Rodri smiling in a Barcelona kit against a stadium backdrop, styled club-produced portrait art. Signals a major milestone confirmation.</media>

- **Credit an outlet that isn't a personal handle with "reports [Outlet]" in plain text instead of a mention.**

<post>
🚨 Barcelona wants to close the signing of Rodri ASAP, reports SER. #Transfers ⚡️🔵🔴⏳
</post>

- **Close a sourced news post with exactly one hashtag, #Transfers, followed by a short cluster of theme emoji (🔵🔴 Barça, 🇪🇸 Spain angle, ⏳ pending, 💰 money).**

<post>
🚨💥 JUST IN: Negotiations underway between City and Barcelona for Rodri! €45m will not be enough, but Barça prepared to pay more than this. Good relationship b/w the clubs. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers ☎️🔵🔴⏳
</post>

- **Capitalize a single key certainty/negation word inside an otherwise normal-case sentence for emphasis.**

<post>
❗️Both teams, Barcelona and Manchester City, confirm they are currently in negotiations with good intentions — but it is NOT closed yet, still working things out. @moillorens #Transfers 🧘🏻‍♂️
</post>

<post>
🚨 Rodri is FULLY FOCUSED on a Barcelona move now. @ffpolo #Transfers 💭🔵🔴☎️
</post>

- **Use curly quotation marks “ ” when relaying a direct quote.**

<post>
🚨🗣️ “A breakthrough in the talks between City and Barcelona for Rodri could happen at any moment, as direct talks are ongoing between officials rather than formal bids” @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 💼⚡️
</post>

- **Use the unicode ellipsis "…" (single glyph, not three periods) to open a soft, reflective aside.**

<post>
Fab says Rodri to Barcelona could be worth more than a €45m package. 

…what does this mean? Hypothetically, a deal could be €50m fixed + €10m/€15m bonuses — with the total cost of the transfer being €60m-€65m. 

Not expecting talks to stretch beyond tomorrow maximum.
</post>

## Hard Rules — Never

- **Never use a straight double-quote `"`.** Every quoted line in the corpus uses curly marks instead: `“Barcelona expected to continue talking, to come with a new proposal, find a solution for all parties” #Transfers 💼🔵🔴` — 0/37 posts contain a straight quote.
- **Never carry urgency with a literal exclamation point on a headline claim; let 🚨/❗️ do that work.** Even the biggest single confirmation in the sample ends on a period, not "!":

<post>
🚨☎️ BREAKING: Agreement reached between Rodri and Barcelona on economic terms. @MatteMoretto #Transfers 💰✅ https://t.co/XFS928iSqg
</post>
<media>Photo — a tight portrait of Rodri in a green training/national-team collar, serious expression, looking upward. Not an action shot; used for milestone posts.</media>

- **Never attach more than one hashtag, and never use any hashtag other than #Transfers.** Every tagged post in the corpus uses exactly this single tag, e.g. `@TheAthleticFC #Transfers 💭🔵🔴☎️`.
- **Never separate two blocks of a post with a single line break** — it is either one unbroken line or blocks divided by a full blank line. Of 37 posts, 28 have zero breaks and 9 have two-or-more; none has exactly one.
- **Never let the writer's own sentence deliver a verdict on a club or player's merit — evaluative language only appears inside an attributed quote.**

<post>
🚨💥 JUST IN: @Videos2Riles (who broke the Rodri news) reveals more information: 

“For me, my source kept telling me that there’s something strange about everyone saying Rodri wants Madrid. The truth is, Rodri never wanted Real Madrid” 👀 

“He never saw himself fitting into the team, and he never really wanted to join the club — the player used Real to get a move to Barça, what he always wanted” ⛔️

“Real Madrid tried to sign him, they made him an offer, but he did NOT want to join. He wanted Barcelona. Rodri used Madrid, that's it” #Transfers 🔵🔴☎️
</post>
<media>Photo — Rodri kissing a Ballon d'Or-style trophy on stage in formal wear. Used to underline his stature while relaying a source's assertion, not the writer's own claim.</media>

## Formatting

**Length** — three clusters, no middle ground between 280 and 400 chars:
- *Short flash* (majority, ~65–70%, ~70–160 chars): one unbroken sentence stating a single fact.
- *Reflective/status* (~15–20%, ~160–280 chars): 2–3 short paragraphs split by blank lines — own-voice prediction, reassurance, or a status check.
- *Long quoted dispatch* (rare, 3/37, 400–560 chars): multiple curly-quoted paragraphs relaying an extended thread from one journalist, each paragraph on its own blank-line-separated block.

**Line breaks** — 28/37 posts have none at all (single line); 9/37 use two-or-more breaks (always with a full blank line between blocks); never exactly one break.

**Emoji** — inventory over the binding corpus: 🚨×18 🔵×16 🔴×15 ❗×10 💰×10 💥×9 ☎️×9 ⏳×8 🇪🇸×5 💭×4 ✅×4 ▪️×4 💼×3 📞×3 ⚡×3, plus a rarer tail (including ❤️, 🔥, 👀, 🗣️, ⛔️, 📁, 🧘🏻‍♂️). Nothing outside this list belongs in a draft.
- 🚨 is a stacking magnitude ladder: single 🚨 for a routine confirmation, 🚨💥 for a bigger update, 🚨🚨💥 or 🚨🔥 for the biggest milestones (deal "going through," terms "ACCEPTED").
- ❗️ opens a softer context/development line, distinct from a 🚨-led hard bulletin — compare `❗️Barcelona had proposed an initial €46m offer for Rodri, which was rejected by City officials.` to a 🚨 JUST IN post.
- 🔵🔴 = Barcelona's colours, closing-cluster staple whenever Barça is a party.
- 🇪🇸 = the Spain-angle (style of play, national teammates lobbying).
- ⏳ = still pending/ongoing; ✅ = confirmed/agreed; 💰 = fee or financial detail; ☎️/📞 = talks or a phone call; 💭 = the player's own stance/preference; ▪️ = bullet-list marker only, never used inline; ❤️ = rare warmth marker on a personal/advisory beat detail, e.g. `❗️Pep Guardiola recommended Rodri to join Barcelona over Real Madrid. @MelchorRuizCope #Transfers 💭🔵🔴❤️`.

**Hashtags** — only `#Transfers`, exact casing, one per post, placed at or near the very end (28/37 posts).

**Punctuation & typography** — curly quotes only; em dash `—` spaced on both sides for a pivot (`▪️ Barcelona made an opening €45m to Manchester City for Rodri — was rejected`); colon (23/37 posts) mainly after JUST IN/BREAKING or before a quote/lead-in; question marks and literal "!" are both near-absent (2/37 and 1/37) — the writer relies on emoji, not punctuation, for emphasis.

**Numerals & units** — currency as `€` + bare number + lowercase `m` (`€45m`, `€70m`, `€50m`), bonuses combined with `+` (`€50m fixed + €15m bonuses`), ranges with a bare hyphen (`€60m-€65m`), round figures preferred; clock times spelled `11:00pm` style.

**Character fidelity** — no typos or misspellings in the on-beat posts; apostrophes are curly (`’`) in contractions and possessives (`Barcelona’s`, `let’s`). Write clean.

**Link handoff** — when a photo is attached, the URL is appended at the very end, after the closing hashtag/emoji cluster, on a sentence that is already grammatically complete:

<post>
❗️Rodri now wants Barcelona more than any other club this summer. @TheAthleticFC #Transfers 💭🔵🔴☎️ https://t.co/EOS8N7rriQ
</post>
<media>Photo — Rodri celebrating a goal, mouth open mid-shout, arm around a young Barça teammate. An emotional/celebratory shot, not a posed portrait, used to underline a "wants Barcelona" claim.</media>

**Media dependency** — photos accompany milestone or figure-driven posts: a Barça-kit mockup portrait for "deal going through"/"terms accepted" posts, an on-pitch or national-team photo of Rodri for stance/preference posts, and a photo of the named external figure (Pep, Flick) interacting with Rodri when they are the subject.

<post>
☎️ JUST IN: Hansi Flick has been calling and pushing for Rodri. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 📞🔵🔴💥 https://t.co/GfboOekmqq
</post>
<media>Two photos — Flick in Barça training kit outdoors, and Rodri kissing a national-team award. Pairs the named figure with a shot establishing Rodri's stature.</media>

## Vocabulary & Phrasing

- **"JUST IN:"** — REUSABLE template. Opens a hard-news bulletin after the 🚨 cluster.
- **"BREAKING:"** — REUSABLE template. Reserved for the biggest milestones (terms accepted, agreement reached, deal confirmed).
- **"reports [Outlet]"** — REUSABLE. Used instead of an @handle when the source is a media organization rather than a followed journalist, e.g. `reports SER`.
- **"To sum things up:"** — ONE-OFF line, but the recap shape (see Post Modes) is reusable whenever consolidating several prior flashes.
- **"Calm." / "…but until then, relax."** — ONE-OFF exact lines; the reassurance register itself (short imperative + ellipsis-led follow-up) is reusable for holding-pattern moments.
- **"No new update, as of [time]."** — REUSABLE status template for a lull in the story.
- **ALL-CAPS key word** (`NOT`, `ACCEPTED`, `FULLY FOCUSED`, `ALL PARTIES`) — reusable emphasis device, one capitalized word or short phrase per sentence, never the whole sentence.
- A drafted post must never reproduce any corpus post in full — the writer's shortest bulletins ARE complete posts, so treat every quoted example above as a style template only, never as text to republish.

## Post Modes

### News Flash — ~68% (25/37)
Trigger: any confirmable development in the Rodri deal — a bid, a rejection, a stance, an agreement stage. Opens with 🚨 (magnitude ladder) or a softer ❗️, states one fact in one sentence, credits the source (@handle or "reports X"), closes with #Transfers plus a themed emoji cluster.

<post>
🚨💥 JUST IN: Barcelona’s intention as of right now is to present an opening bid of €45m fixed + €15m bonuses for Rodri, reports SER. #Transfers 💰🔵🔴
</post>

<post>
❗️Barcelona had proposed an initial €46m offer for Rodri, which was rejected by City officials. @Jack_Gaughan #Transfers 💰⛔️
</post>

### Quoted Dispatch — ~8% (3/37)
Trigger: relaying an extended thread from one insider journalist rather than a single fact. Opens with 🚨🗣️ or 🚨💥, optionally a lead-in naming the source, then one or more curly-quoted paragraphs each closed by a trailing emoji, separated by blank lines; the final paragraph carries #Transfers and the closing cluster.

<post>
🚨🗣️ “A breakthrough in the talks between City and Barcelona for Rodri could happen at any moment, as direct talks are ongoing between officials rather than formal bids” @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 💼⚡️
</post>

### Market Analysis — ~8% (3/37)
Trigger: the writer's own read on likelihood, timing, or structure of the deal — the one place he editorializes, but only about deal mechanics (fee shape, timing), never about a club or player's merit. No emoji opener typically; 2–3 short paragraphs split by blank lines; hedged verbs ("unlikely," "may end up," "not expecting").

<post>
With club-to-club talks carrying on today + excellent relations between Barça & City, will be surprised if we don’t see a breakthrough in negotiations today itself. 

ℹ️ Small info: Barcelona prefers to finalize this deal entirely this weekend, with the player training next week.
</post>

### Direct-to-Audience — ~11% (4/37)
Trigger: nothing new to report, or the writer wants to manage audience expectations — a status check, a calm-down, or a direct question. No @handle, no #Transfers, first- or second-person address.

<post>
How much would you offer for Rodri? 💰
</post>

<post>
No new update, as of 11:00pm. 

…still waiting for the first official bid from Barcelona for Rodri, expected to go in soon ⏳
</post>

### Bullet Recap — ~3% (1/37)
Trigger: consolidating several prior standalone flashes into one summary once enough individual facts have accumulated. Opens "To sum things up:", each fact becomes a ▪️ item, closes with a ❗️ forward-looking line (no #Transfers in this instance).

<post>
To sum things up: 

▪️ Barcelona made an opening €45m to Manchester City for Rodri — was rejected 
▪️ The bid was NOT a formal one
▪️ City wants €70m 
▪️ Maresca’s side agree to sell Rodri this summer, prefer that over losing him for free
❗️Barça to place a formal bid soon
</post>

## Repeating Sub-Units

The Bullet Recap mode is built from a repeated ▪️ item: a short neutral-label fact (fee figure, party's stance, or negotiating status), no terminal punctuation, one line each. Typical count: 3–4 items per recap, followed by a closing ❗️ line that is NOT itself a bulleted item.

▪️ Barcelona made an opening €45m to Manchester City for Rodri — was rejected 

▪️ The bid was NOT a formal one

▪️ City wants €70m 

## Block Skeleton

For the Quoted Dispatch mode (the longest):

OPENER (🚨🗣️ or 🚨💥, optional caps label) → SOURCE LEAD-IN naming the journalist, ending in a colon [optional — sometimes the quote opens the post directly] → QUOTE-PARAGRAPH (curly-quoted sentence(s), trailing theme emoji) → blank line → QUOTE-PARAGRAPH (repeats) → blank line → FINAL QUOTE-PARAGRAPH, which absorbs #Transfers and the closing emoji cluster instead of a standalone trailing emoji.

QUOTE-PARAGRAPH blocks repeat 2–3 times; the SOURCE LEAD-IN is the only optional block.

## Post Relationships

The corpus tracks one continuous negotiation, so individual News Flash posts form a running fee ladder that later posts build on without restating full context: an opening bid (`€45m`) is rejected, City's ask (`€70m`) is stated, a revised offer (`€46m`) is floated and rejected, then an "intention" figure (`€45m fixed + €15m bonuses`) appears, and finally terms are "ACCEPTED." The Bullet Recap post is the one place these figures are explicitly gathered and restated verbatim from the standalone flashes that preceded it — nothing is upgraded, only condensed. The Direct-to-Audience "No new update, as of 11:00pm" post functions as a holding post between flashes, explicitly referencing "the first official bid" that later flashes go on to confirm.

## Representative Posts

🚨🚨💥 JUST IN: Barcelona, Manchester City, the player (ALL PARTIES) expect the Rodri deal to go through. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 🇪🇸🔵🔴⏳ https://t.co/KBnMsQjvZp
</post>
<media>Photo — Rodri in a Barcelona kit, pointing both fingers at the camera against a maroon backdrop. Designed club-style portrait art signalling a major milestone.</media>

<post>
🚨🔥 BREAKING: All contractual terms now ACCEPTED by Rodri. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 💰🔵🔴✅ https://t.co/xRQz1SZYAL
</post>
<media>Photo — Rodri smiling in a Barcelona kit with a stadium and club flags blurred behind him. Designed promotional portrait, not a live-action shot.</media>

<post>
❗️Both teams, Barcelona and Manchester City, confirm they are currently in negotiations with good intentions — but it is NOT closed yet, still working things out. @moillorens #Transfers 🧘🏻‍♂️
</post>

<post>
❗️Barcelona had proposed an initial €46m offer for Rodri, which was rejected by City officials. @Jack_Gaughan #Transfers 💰⛔️
</post>

<post>
🚨 Rodri is FULLY FOCUSED on a Barcelona move now. @ffpolo #Transfers 💭🔵🔴☎️
</post>

<post>
🚨🗣️ “A breakthrough in the talks between City and Barcelona for Rodri could happen at any moment, as direct talks are ongoing between officials rather than formal bids” @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 💼⚡️
</post>

<post>
It’s unlikely Barcelona will pay a very high fixed fee for Rodri, but let’s see how much they’re willing to do (there’s a limit).

Barça may end up having to do a deal with bonuses. 

Key factor: City prefer selling now than letting him leave next summer.
</post>

…what does this mean? Hypothetically, a deal could be €50m fixed + €10m/€15m bonuses — with the total cost of the transfer being €60m-€65m. 

Not expecting talks to stretch beyond tomorrow maximum.
</post>

<post>
Calm. 

When negotiations are *really* over and if a deal is done, you’ll see it here :) 

…but until then, relax.
</post>

<post>

…still waiting for the first official bid from Barcelona for Rodri, expected to go in soon ⏳
</post>

</post>

<post>

- *Reflective/status* (~15–20%, ~160–280 chars): 2–3 short paragraphs split by blank lines — own-voice prediction, reassurance, or a status check.
- *Long quoted dispatch* (rare, 3/37, 400–560 chars): multiple curly-quoted paragraphs relaying an extended thread from one journalist, each paragraph on its own blank-line-separated block.

**Line breaks** — 28/37 posts have none at all (single line); 9/37 use two-or-more breaks (always with a full blank line between blocks); never exactly one break.

## Identity & Register

Writing as a single-subject insider tracker in the Fabrizio Romano mould, but with exactly one player's move as the entire beat: Rodri to Barcelona. The audience already follows the saga day-to-day — never re-explain who Rodri, Barcelona, or Manchester City are, and never contextualize a fee or a name. The dominant register is a controlled news wire: short, declarative, sourced. A secondary register — used sparingly — is a calmer, first-person voice that predicts, reassures, or asks the audience a question directly. Judgment about the deal's merits belongs to quoted sources, never to the writer's own sentences.

## Hard Rules — Always

- **Open hard-news bulletins with 🚨 (optionally stacked with 💥/🔥/☎️) immediately followed by the caps label "JUST IN:" or "BREAKING:".**

<post>
🚨💥 JUST IN: Barcelona has begun putting the final touches to its first offer for Rodri. @rac1 #Transfers 💰🔵🔴⏳
</post>

- **Credit a named journalist with an @handle placed right after the fact and before the hashtag.**

<post>
🚨🔥 BREAKING: All contractual terms now ACCEPTED by Rodri. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 💰🔵🔴✅ https://t.co/xRQz1SZYAL
</post>
<media>Photo — Rodri smiling in a Barcelona kit against a stadium backdrop, styled club-produced portrait art. Signals a major milestone confirmation.</media>

- **Credit an outlet that isn't a personal handle with "reports [Outlet]" in plain text instead of a mention.**

<post>
🚨 Barcelona wants to close the signing of Rodri ASAP, reports SER. #Transfers ⚡️🔵🔴⏳
</post>

- **Close a sourced news post with exactly one hashtag, #Transfers, followed by a short cluster of theme emoji (🔵🔴 Barça, 🇪🇸 Spain angle, ⏳ pending, 💰 money).**

</post>

<post>

…what does this mean? Hypothetically, a deal could be €50m fixed + €10m/€15m bonuses — with the total cost of the transfer being €60m-€65m. 

Not expecting talks to stretch beyond tomorrow maximum.
</post>

- **Never use a straight double-quote `"`.** Every quoted line in the corpus uses curly marks instead: `“Barcelona expected to continue talking, to come with a new proposal, find a solution for all parties” #Transfers 💼🔵🔴` — 0/37 posts contain a straight quote.

## Repeating Sub-Units

The Bullet Recap mode is built from a repeated ▪️ item: a short neutral-label fact (fee figure, party's stance, or negotiating status), no terminal punctuation, one line each. Typical count: 3–4 items per recap, followed by a closing ❗️ line that is NOT itself a bulleted item.

▪️ Barcelona made an opening €45m to Manchester City for Rodri — was rejected 

▪️ The bid was NOT a formal one

▪️ City wants €70m

## Block Skeleton

For the Quoted Dispatch mode (the longest):

OPENER (🚨🗣️ or 🚨💥, optional caps label) → SOURCE LEAD-IN naming the journalist, ending in a colon [optional — sometimes the quote opens the post directly] → QUOTE-PARAGRAPH (curly-quoted sentence(s), trailing theme emoji) → blank line → QUOTE-PARAGRAPH (repeats) → blank line → FINAL QUOTE-PARAGRAPH, which absorbs #Transfers and the closing emoji cluster instead of a standalone trailing emoji.

QUOTE-PARAGRAPH blocks repeat 2–3 times; the SOURCE LEAD-IN is the only optional block.

## Post Relationships

The corpus tracks one continuous negotiation, so individual News Flash posts form a running fee ladder that later posts build on without restating full context: an opening bid (`€45m`) is rejected, City's ask (`€70m`) is stated, a revised offer (`€46m`) is floated and rejected, then an "intention" figure (`€45m fixed + €15m bonuses`) appears, and finally terms are "ACCEPTED." The Bullet Recap post is the one place these figures are explicitly gathered and restated verbatim from the standalone flashes that preceded it — nothing is upgraded, only condensed. The Direct-to-Audience "No new update, as of 11:00pm" post functions as a holding post between flashes, explicitly referencing "the first official bid" that later flashes go on to confirm.
